correctness.rationale: Four restricted Walsh characters are orthogonal iff their six nonzero pairwise frequencies lie in joint Fourier-zero Z. Plane cosets b+W give 2^(d-2)T. For independent B=b+{0,x,y,z}, six distinct nonzero directions of H=span(x,y,z) lie in Z, leaving t=x+y+z. For each four-point A, the binary evaluation map H->F2^2 (plane time set) or F2^3 (independent time set) has image rank <=2; its kernel cannot contain any of the six zero directions, hence is exactly {0,t}; t annihilates all time differences. Conversely t in joint annihilator I and admissible W span H of dimension 3 and yield six zeros. Counting four complements W for each (H,t), eight independent unordered quadruples of prescribed nonzero four-sum in each 8-point H coset, yields N_ind=2^(d-2)(2^h-1)T, total 2^(d+h-2)T. d=2 forces h=0. Independent direct finite binary enumeration checks the seven obstruction subfamilies counts 16,16,4,16,4,4,0; finite tests corroborate rather than prove the universal law.
